links.comparator_used: Direct deployment of the Lead-I model, trained on hospital ECGs, to Apple Watch and QOCA ECG102D consumer ECGs without fine-tuning
links.outcome: AUC across eight classification tasks on consumer single-lead ECGs (Apple Watch, QOCA ECG102D)
links.effect: Direct deployment produced substantial accuracy losses. After fine-tuning, AUCs were significantly improved: low EF 0.85/0.86, elevated PASP 0.73/0.68, anemia 0.73/0.69 (Apple Watch/QOCA).
links.tradeoff: Fine-tuning needs about 500-1000 labeled ECGs to be reliable, and smaller sets can be harmful. Performance was lower in atrial fibrillation than in sinus rhythm.
links.quote: After fine-tuning, AUCs across eight classification tasks for the Apple Watch and QOCA ECG102D were significantly improved, with high performance for low EF (0.85/0.86) and more modest performance for elevated PASP (0.73/0.68) and anemia (0.73/0.69).

design_hint: local fine-tuning/recalibration on target-device data before deployment
